disagreementsResolved: No count differs between A and B. Both give the same used lists per branch (main 95, WP3 87, WP4 100, WP5 110, WP6 90) and the same behindSwitchOff lists (14, 0, 0, 7, 1). Both report the same 5 liveOnly entries, the same declared-but-never-called entry (WP6 socket-halts), a union of 186 and the same 31 uncovered paths. My own pass reproduces every figure. I extracted each ref with git archive, imported its registry, walked the import closure from worker.js and scripts/flows-pipeline.mjs, and read the call sites of every id: wrapper calls for WP4's ask(id), table jobs for WP5 and WP6, and the dossier's sourceOf.

Stale main: both counts read origin/main at b0b6e7c, but after the fetch origin/main is dfe0cad (#285, Market Floor funds). I re-derived main at dfe0cad. It still has 100 registry entries (the commit only adds BUDGETS.funds) and the same 95 spec paths, 14 of them behind switches. The funds read moved from the Actions live leg to a new Worker cron (2-57/5 13-21 MON-FRI) and an on-demand fill behind /api/flows/lk. Both paths it reads, /api/screener/stocks and /api/market/sector-etfs, were already used, so no count changes.

WebSocket, where A and B describe the same call differently. A filed the rail's upgrade under calledOutsideRegistry as '/api/socket' plus four '/api/socket/<channel>' paths, and said counting them would give 191 used and 26 uncovered. B said the upgrade goes to /socket, which is not a spec path. The code agrees with B. socketUrl in shared/flows-rt-socket.js sets the pathname to '/socket' (wss://<feed host>/socket?token=...), and that file is the same on all five branches. The spec's GET /api/socket is a separate REST endpoint that lists channels, and nothing calls it. The entries /api/socket/price, /gex, /flow_alerts and /news document channels the rail joins, but no request goes to those paths. I kept the stricter reading: none of the 19 /api/socket* paths counts as used. If joined channels were counted, the union would be 190 (B's figure), not 191.

WP5 owner-only route name: A wrote /api/flows/macro-now and B wrote /api/flows/macro/now. The route row is /api/flows/macro/now (server/routes/flows-macro.js:103), behind FLOWS_MACRO=owner and FLOWS_MACRO_LIVE=owner. 'macro-now' is only its cache-key namespace. No count changes: the 7 paths reached only from buildMacroNow (fx-rate, crypto-state, futures-trades, digital-intraday, crypto-whales, crypto-whale-tx, fx-intraday) stay in behindSwitchOff.

Main live for members: 95 - 14 = 81. Of the 14, 12 are Flow Lab reads in server/flowlab.js, reachable only through /api/flows/flowlab/* behind FLOWS_FLOWLAB=owner. The other 2 are /api/analytics/window and /api/analytics/sliding, which the nightly runs only when FLOWS_FLOWLAB_ANALYTICS is exactly 'on'; wrangler.toml sets it to 'off' and the workflow does not pass it. Of the remaining 81, 4 are nightly Flow Lab reads whose payloads only the owner can open while FLOWS_FLOWLAB=owner: /api/option-trades/optionable-tickers, /api/option-trades/exchange-breakdown/{date}, /api/screener/option-contracts and /api/group-flow/{flow_group}/greek-flow/{expiry}. They still count as live by the definition, because no wrangler.toml switch gates their nightly call sites.

After the train: 186 of 217 paths are used (85.7%), and 186 of 218 operations. Every use is a GET, so 32 operations stay uncovered: the 31 uncovered GETs and the one POST. 22 of the 186 sit behind wrangler.toml switches: 20 owner-only (12 Flow Lab, 7 WP5 macro live, 1 WP6 quote) and 2 off (analytics), which leaves 164. Another 15 WP6 paths run only when the repository variable FLOWS_EVENTRISK_NIGHTLY is set, and the workflow defaults it to 'off'. That leaves 149 paths requested by default by members or by scheduled jobs with no switch. Repository variables cannot be read statically.

More registry entries than paths, because some entries share a spec path. In WP5, economy and treasury-yield both resolve to /api/economy/{indicator}: 111 in-spec entries for 110 paths. In WP6, listings-active and listings-delisted both resolve to /api/companies/listings: 91 entries for 90 paths. ohlc-1d, treasury-yield and tech-natr match through their op templates. The POST on /api/alerts/configuration creates or updates an alert configuration on the account. WP6's alerts-config entry is a GET, so no branch writes anything.

newVsMain: every package branch forked at 36c1ea1, where 74 paths were used, and each keeps all 74. Main has added 21 since (#282, #283). WP3 adds 13 paths, all in the voldesk nightly. WP4 adds 26: 22 through its ask(id) wrapper and 4 as extras ps parts. WP5 adds 36 from 37 entries. WP6 adds 16 from 18 entries, after dropping socket-halts and the duplicate listings path. No new path overlaps another branch's or main's 21. WP3 and WP4 have nothing behind switches: their reads run in the nightly under repository variables that default to on (FLOWS_VOLDESK_BUILD, FLOWS_POSITIONING_NIGHTLY). FLOWS_VOLDESK=owner and FLOWS_POSITIONING=owner only close the pages and read routes.
confidence: High. Three derivations agree on every figure (A by registry, B by call site, and mine with independent scripts), and mine was rerun on the current origin/main. The SHAs counted are main dfe0cad, WP3 3ccce72, WP4 8ed8d6a, WP5 efbd05f and WP6 2d5e6f2. The spec docs/uw-openapi.yaml is the same blob on all five branches (217 paths: 217 GET plus 1 POST). Caveats: the figures hold only for these SHAs, and WP3 is being merged now. The union assumes each package merges with its calls intact. Repository variables (vars.*) cannot be read statically and could change the nightly gates. My scripts and outputs are in <scratchpad>/census-reconcile/ (census.mjs, union.mjs, data/union.json, data/census-*.json).
